sections.report:
**First read.** My eye lands on "Library opening hours" at the top left, then drops down three bold branch names, each with two lines of times or places. It's a plain web page of opening hours for a small public library system. It feels calm, neutral and functional. The right 60% of the frame is empty.

**Job (assumed).** The page tells local residents when and where they can visit each library branch.

**Walk, The whole piece**
- Purpose clear in one sentence: yes
- Main image and headline make one idea: yes (there's no image, so the line doesn't apply)
- Every element does a job: yes
- One mood and era: yes
- Copy finished, no placeholder or spelling mistakes: unsure. There's no placeholder text and no misspelling. But the Mobile library block (y≈425–491) gives a day and a place and no time, so it reads as an unfinished draft, and those are details people act on.
- Repeated elements look the same: yes
- Colors, shapes and directions carry the right mood: yes
- Each heading names its section: yes

That copy line has no catalog entry, so there are no entries to open. After weighing it, I answer **no**.

---

**Section.** The whole piece: applies.

**Findings**
1. **Is the copy finished, with no placeholder text and no spelling mistakes?** No. The Mobile library block at about x 96–376, y 425–491 reads "Wednesday at the market square" and "Thursday at the school gates" with no time. The two branches above give hours, so a reader expects the same here and finds a gap. They know which day to go but not when, so they can turn up and miss the van, which is exactly what an hours page should prevent. "Nine to eight" and "ten to four" also leave a.m./p.m. unstated. Common sense fixes that one, but "ten to six" can also be read as the clock time 5:50, which matters on a page people plan their trip around. This line has no catalog source, so it's common sense. **Defect. Weight: major.** Fix: give every mobile stop a start and end time, the way the branches have them. Write all times so they can only be read one way, for example "9 am to 8 pm" or "09:00–20:00". Also say which days each branch is closed. Right now "closed on Sunday" is only implied by leaving Sunday out.

**What's working.**
- **One thing, said once.** Apart from the title, the page has three blocks with the same structure: a bold place name, then two plain lines. There is no ornament or extra chrome. Anyone can tell at a glance that this is an hours list, and the bold names let them jump straight to their branch.
- **Headings name what they hold.** "Main branch", "Harbour branch" and "Mobile library" are the words a resident would scan for, so nobody has to decode labels.

**Checklist.** The whole piece: 8 lines, 7 yes, 1 no (copy finished: mobile library times missing, and times can be read two ways)

Walk (working notes). There were no crops: the image is 1280×800, about one screen, and Bash was refused, so I worked from the whole image.

First read: the eye lands on "Library opening hours" at top left, then moves down three bold labels, each with two lines under it. It reads as a plain hours notice for a public library. It feels calm and sparse, with the right two-thirds empty.

Job, assumed: show library visitors when and where each branch is open.

What matters first:
- One element dominates: yes. The title (about 28 px bold, y≈60–95) is clearly the largest and heaviest.
- Distinct levels below it: yes. There are three levels: title, branch labels (about 18 px bold), and hours (about 18 px regular). The labels match the body size and differ by weight alone, which is enough at a glance. No two sizes are close.
- Larger headings also differ in weight, form or colour: yes. The title is larger and also bold. The branch labels are not larger, so they differ by weight only, which is the right tool at that level.

There are no `no` or `unsure` lines, so there are no entries to open.

**Section.** What matters first (hierarchy): applies.

**Findings**
None.

**What's working.**
- The title (x≈96–397, y≈60–95) is the only large element, and it is about 1.5× the body size and bold. The eye knows where to start, and the title says what the page is at once.
- The branch labels ("Main branch" y≈143, "Harbour branch" y≈284, "Mobile library" y≈425) are the same size as the hours and differ only in weight. That gives a clear second level without a fourth size. It follows the "bolder, not bigger" approach (Wathan and Schoger, *Refactoring UI*), and a reader can scan down the labels to find their branch.

**Checklist.** What matters first: 3 lines, 3 yes, 0 no, 0 unsure.

sections.report:
**Section.** Arrangement and space: applies.

**Findings**
1. **Does the visual weight balance, with no side, crowded or empty, that makes the page look about to tip?** No.
   - **Where:** All the content sits in a narrow column in the top-left corner, about x 96–400 and y 60–500 of the 1280×800 frame. The right ~880 px and the bottom ~300 px are empty, so roughly three quarters of the frame is blank and nothing on that side carries any weight.
   - **What the viewer experiences:** The page tips up and to the left. As a whole screen it reads like a layout that didn't load or a block that lost its container, not like a finished page. The hours are still easy to read, but the page looks unfinished, and that costs some trust.
   - **Why:** Where an element sits changes its weight, and a heavy side needs a counterweight (Arnheim, *Art and Visual Perception*, ch. I "Balance").
   - **Direction of the fix:** Give the column a container sized to its content so the void reads as a margin, or let the three branches use the width (for example, side by side in columns). Either way the empty area should look intended, not left over. If this frame is a crop of a wider page that has other content on the right, this is not a finding.
   - **Kind and weight:** Convention. Minor, because the information still gets through. It becomes major if this is the whole screen users see.

**What's working.**
- **Grouping by space:** Lines inside each branch are about 33 px apart, while the gaps between branches are about 55 px. Each bold heading sits tight on its own two lines, so the three branches read as three units at a glance, with no rules or boxes needed (Wertheimer's proximity, via Arnheim ch. II).
- **One left edge:** The title, headings and lines all hang from x=96 with no near-misses, so the column reads as one deliberate stack.

**Checklist.** Arrangement and space: 13 lines, 12 yes, 1 no (visual weight balances). I could not run the crop script because Bash was denied, so I judged from the whole image, which fits on one screen.

Walk (Text, 30 lines): body text large enough (about 18 px), yes. Captions large enough, yes. Plain upright face, yes. One family (sans, bold and regular), yes. Small text weight holds up, yes. Contrast 4.5:1 (near-black on white), yes. Text over image: none, yes. Lines 45 to 75 characters: no paragraphs, only short lines, yes. Line spacing suits the line length, yes. Multi-line heading: none, yes. Flush left, yes. Justified: none, yes. Rag: short list lines, yes. Widows: none, yes. Heading breaks, yes. Paragraph marks: groups set off by space only, yes. Crisp left edge at x≈96, yes. Chunked by branch, yes. Mixed case, yes. Emphasis (bold only on branch names), yes. Display tighter: the 30 px heading looks set at default spacing but reads tight enough, yes. Kerning, yes. Letter spacing, yes. Caps letterspacing: none, yes. Ligatures: no fi/fl at a large size, yes. Real bold, yes. Quotes and dashes: none, yes. Tabular figures: none, yes. Real type, yes. Nothing clipped, yes.

No line came out `no` or `unsure`, so there was no step 5 to run.

**Section.** Text: applies.

**Findings**
None.

(Not a checklist line, a copy note for the director: the opening hours are things people act on, and the words leave gaps. The mobile library at y≈458 and y≈491 gives a day and a place but **no times**, so someone can't plan to meet it. "Nine to eight" and "ten to four" (y≈176 to 350) are spelled out in words. They're harder to scan than "9:00–20:00" and could be misread as "ten minutes to four". Mark it a **defect, major** for the mobile library line: someone can't act on it. Mark it **taste, minor** for words versus numbers. Fix: give the mobile library its hours, and write all the times as numbers with an en dash.)

**What's working.** Each branch is one tight block: a bold name and two regular lines at even spacing (about 33 px), with roughly twice that gap between blocks (about 75 px). So the three blocks read as separate at a glance, using only weight and space. The type uses one sans family in two weights and about three sizes, all near-black on white, which keeps it quiet and very easy to read.

**Checklist.** Text: 30 lines, 30 yes, 0 no, 0 unsure

**Walk (working notes).** First read: the bold title "Library opening hours" at top left, then the three bold branch names, then the hours under each one. It reads as a plain, calm notice for library users. Everything is near-black text on white, with no hue anywhere.
Color: small palette yes · saturated color kept small yes (none) · light/dark range yes · warm forward, cool back yes (no hues) · matched colors look the same yes · no vibrating edges yes · status colors yes (none) · color not alone in carrying meaning yes · dark theme yes (light theme, does not apply). There were no `no` or `unsure` lines, so there was no deep read.

---

**Section.** Color: applies. The piece is entirely neutral, with near-black text on a white background.

**Findings**
None.

**What's working.**
- **Value does all the work.** Near-black text on pure white has strong contrast. The levels (title, branch names, hours) come from weight and size, not color, so the piece keeps its structure in grayscale and needs nothing from color.
- **Restraint suits the job.** A schedule notice with no status or category to show gets no benefit from an accent color. Not having one means nothing competes with the hours.

**Checklist.** Color: 9 lines, 9 yes, 0 no, 0 unsure

**Section.** Pictures: skipped. The image is text only: a heading and three blocks of branch hours, black type on white. It has no photos, illustrations, icons, logos or marks, and no empty placeholder box or broken-image icon either. The blank area on the right and at the bottom is empty background, not a missing picture.

**Findings**
None.

**Checklist.** Pictures: skipped
